newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean shares end firm, but undertone weak.
newsitem.headline: Chilean shares end firm, but undertone weak.

text.p: Chilean blue chips closed a shade higher, but weak foreign demand and a lack of local news are likely to send stocks tumbling next week, said traders.
"As long as there is no news and no foreign buyers, Chile will trade mixed to lower," said one broker at a foreign bank.
The 40-share index closed up 0.07 percent at 131.63 points. The general index gained 0.23 percent to 5,729.51 points.
Turnover was 10.2 billion pesos, similar to Thursday's level.
Winners included pulp and paper producers, which climbed on speculation that cellulose prices could soon start to rise, said dealers.
But the rally, which has buoyed the bolsa for much of the week, could lose steam next week unless there is evidence that cellulose prices are actually firming, said one broker.
"The rally looks overdone as stocks have run ahead of themselves without any moves in pulp prices," he said.
Copec, Chile's top pulp producer, ended up 1.9 percent at 2,150 pesos. Paper-maker CMPC climbed 1.94 percent to 5,250 pesos.
Fertilizer-maker Soquimich continued its two-day bull run on media reports that the firm's low lithium prices may drive competitors into the ground, leaving it with a world monopoly, said traders.
But that rally could soon fade.
"The stock is way too high as earnings growth this year is not that impressive," said one trader.
Soquimich ended up 3.85 percent at 2,700 pesos.

Losers included copper products maker Madeco, down 2.86 percent at 1,020 pesos, and winery Concha y Toro, which shed 1.85 percent at 265 pesos. ((-- Margaret Orgill, Santiago newsroom, 562-699-5595x212))
